Maserati new model range: Grecale, GranTurismo and GranCabrio
The updated Maserati Grecale gets a revised front-end design inspired by the MCPURA, along with a new 390bhp V6 engine option derived from the Nettuno powertrain. The electric Grecale Folgore also gets improvements to its driving range. Prices for the new Grecale start at Rs 1.14 crore (ex-showroom).
The GranTurismo and GranCabrio receive revised exterior styling, including a more aggressive front-end design. In the Trofeo versions, the 3.0-litre Nettuno V6 produces up to 590bhp. The electric Folgore versions also benefit from an 80km increase in WLTP range, taking the claimed figure to over 540km.
The updates extend to the interiors, with the three models receiving a new racing-inspired steering wheel, an updated digital clock with an octagonal bezel, a redesigned gear selector and revised digital interfaces.
Maserati has also expanded its Fuoriserie personalisation programme, adding new exterior colours, trim options and coordinated badges. Customers can also opt for bespoke customisation of the GranCabrio's fabric soft-top.
The GT2 Stradale made its India debut at the event and was displayed alongside the updated model range. Based on the Maserati GT2 race car, it brings the brand's motorsport technology to a road-legal performance car.
Power comes from a 3.0-litre twin-turbocharged Nettuno V6 engine producing 640hp, with power sent to the rear wheels. Built in Modena, Italy, the GT2 Stradale sits among the most performance-focused models in Maserati's road-car portfolio.
The model follows Maserati's return to international GT racing through its GT2 programme and represents the road-going interpretation of that racing effort.
